knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r}
library(nososim)
devtools::load_all()
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Define patient and staff landscapes

`make_landscape()` gives one row per location, with a `capacity` column.
Patients occupy beds in rooms, so their landscape has three levels: hospital,
ward, and room.

```{r}
hospital <- list(
  Geneva = list(
    ICU = c(a = 2, b = 3),
    General = c(a = 1, b = 4, c = 2)
  ),
  Gallen = list(
    ICU = c(a = 3, b = 5),
    General = c(a = 2, b = 4, c = 1)
  )
)
patient_landscape <- make_landscape(hospital)
patient_landscape
```

Staff are assigned to wards, so their landscape stops at the second level.
Here, capacity represents staff positions rather than patient beds.

```{r}
staff_landscape <- make_landscape(list(
  Geneva = c(ICU = 2, General = 3),
  Gallen = c(ICU = 3, General = 4)
))
staff_landscape
```

## Define patient admissions and individuals

Each day, the admission function receives the landscape with an `available`
column and returns one integer count per row, between 0 and `available`.
Here, each free bed fills with probability `filling_prob`.

```{r}
patient_landscape <- patient_landscape |>
  mutate(
    filling_prob = case_when(
      level_1 == "Geneva" & level_2 == "ICU" ~ 0.9,
      level_1 == "Geneva" & level_2 == "General" ~ 0.7,
      level_1 == "Gallen" & level_2 == "ICU" ~ 0.8,
      level_1 == "Gallen" & level_2 == "General" ~ 0.5
    )
  )

patient_admissions <- function(landscape, date) {
  rbinom(
    nrow(landscape),
    size = landscape$available,
    prob = landscape$filling_prob
  )
}
```

The `individuals()` argument takes a function that adds attributes and dates to
one row per admitted person. It preserves their location columns and supplies
`start` (today) and `end` (the last day present, inclusive). Here, each admission
gets a unique patient ID and a length of stay depending on the ward.

```{r}
patient_individuals <- function(admitted, date) {
  admitted |>
    mutate(
      id = paste0("patient_", format(date, "%Y%m%d"), "_", row_number()),
      age = sample(18:90, n(), replace = TRUE),
      role = "patient",
      los = case_when(
        level_2 == "ICU" ~ sample(3:7, n(), replace = TRUE),
        level_2 == "General" ~ sample(5:10, n(), replace = TRUE)
      ),
      start = date,
      end = start + los - 1L
    )
}
```

## Define staff attendance and individuals

Create a fixed roster, then randomly choose two days off per person in each
Monday–Sunday week. Staff keep the same ID across shifts.

```{r}
dates <- seq(as.Date("2024-01-01"), as.Date("2024-01-30"), by = "day")

set.seed(123)
staff_schedule <- staff_landscape |>
  tidyr::uncount(capacity) |>
  mutate(id = paste0("staff_", row_number())) |>
  tidyr::crossing(week = unique(as.Date(cut(dates, "week"))), weekday = 1:7) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5, by = c(id, week)) |>
  transmute(level_1, level_2, id, date = week + weekday - 1L)

staff_on_duty <- function(date) {
  staff_schedule |>
    filter(date == .env$date) |>
    select(level_1, level_2, id)
}
```

Five working days per full week give each person two days off. Only shifts
within `dates` are simulated.

```{r}
staff_attendance <- function(landscape, date) {
  landscape |>
    left_join(
      count(staff_on_duty(date), level_1, level_2),
      by = c("level_1", "level_2")
    ) |>
    mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0L)) |>
    pull(n)
}

staff_individuals <- function(admitted, date) {
  admitted |>
    distinct(level_1, level_2) |>
    left_join(staff_on_duty(date), by = c("level_1", "level_2")) |>
    mutate(role = "staff", start = date, end = date)
}
```

## Generate the populations

`make_population()` calls the attendance and individual functions on each day.
Capacity becomes available on the day after `end`. The two groups have their
own capacities and attendance rules.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
patients <- make_population(
  patient_landscape,
  dates,
  admissions = patient_admissions,
  individuals = patient_individuals
)

staff <- make_population(
  staff_landscape,
  dates,
  admissions = staff_attendance,
  individuals = staff_individuals
)
```

## Plot stays and shifts

Each plot row represents one unit of capacity, grouped by location. Patient
stays and staff shifts run from `start` through `end` (inclusive); grey lines
show unused capacity. Plot each population using its own landscape.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
autoplot(patients, aes(colour = id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(staff, aes(x = start, y = id, colour = id)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = end + 1, yend = id), linewidth = 2) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(level_1, level_2),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Combine patient and staff records

```{r}
population <- bind_rows(
  tibble::as_tibble(patients),
  tibble::as_tibble(staff)
)

population |>
  select(id, starts_with("level_"), age, role, start, end) |>
  group_by(role) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Define daily contacts and weights

`get_contacts()` selects the people present on a date. In this example:

- Two patients can contact only when sharing the same hospital, ward, and room.
- Any pair involving staff can contact anywhere within the same hospital.
- People in different hospitals cannot contact.

```{r}
contact_date <- dates[1]

contact_rule <- function(i, j) {
  same_hospital <- i$level_1 == j$level_1
  same_ward <- i$level_2 == j$level_2
  same_room <- i$level_3 == j$level_3
  either_staff <- i$role == "staff" | j$role == "staff"

  same_hospital & (either_staff | (same_ward & same_room))
}
```

Weights set the intensity of allowed contacts. Here, `level_2` weights wards
and `role` weights patients and staff. Matrix rows are sources; columns are
recipients. The ward and role coefficients multiply without normalisation.
Excluded contacts always remain zero.

```{r}
weights <- list(
  level_2 = matrix(
    c(2, 1, 3, 1),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(c("ICU", "General"), c("ICU", "General"))
  ),
  role = matrix(
    c(1, 2, 1, 1),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(c("patient", "staff"), c("patient", "staff"))
  )
)

contact_matrices <- list(
  unweighted = NULL,
  role_weighted = weights["role"],
  location_weighted = weights["level_2"],
  all_weighted = weights
) |>
  purrr::map(function(w) {
    get_contacts(population, contact_date, by = contact_rule, weights = w)
  })
```

For example, a contact from General staff to an ICU patient in the same hospital
has weight `3 * 1 = 3`; the reverse direction has weight `1 * 2 = 2`.
These cross-ward weights affect only pairs involving staff, since patients in
different wards cannot contact each other.

## Compare contact weights

The four panels share the same people, ordering, and colour scale.
Nested axis labels group people by ward and hospital.

```{r contact-comparison, fig.width=13, fig.height=14}
labels <- population |>
  filter(start <= contact_date, end >= contact_date) |>
  arrange(level_1, level_2, role, level_3, id) |>
  transmute(id, label = paste(id, level_2, level_1, sep = "\r")) |>
  tibble::deframe()

contact_matrices |>
  purrr::imap_dfr(function(values, label) {
    as.data.frame(as.table(values)) |>
      setNames(c("source", "recipient", "intensity")) |>
      mutate(matrix = factor(label, levels = names(contact_matrices)))
  }) |>
  ggplot(aes(recipient, source, fill = intensity)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = names(labels), labels = labels,
    guide = legendry::guide_axis_nested(
      key = "\r", drop_zero = FALSE,
      levels_text = list(
        element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
        element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1),
        element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1)
      )
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = rev(names(labels)), labels = labels,
    guide = legendry::guide_axis_nested(key = "\r", drop_zero = FALSE)
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166AC", name = "Contact intensity") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "Recipient", y = "Source") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
